fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar link <a> <b> depends_on` can silently record a different edge than the one requested, and can produce an edge in which a ticket blocks its own subtree. Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 hit this while wiring epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864's dependency graph: an epic ended up `depends_on` its own child, the requested child-level dependency was never recorded at all, and the operator had to retype children and hand-unlink the bad edge. Self-blocking edges distort `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade, so parallel agents are handed a wrong work order.

The cause is a policy defect rather than a coding slip. `resolve_hierarchy_link` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98`) decides "comparable level" for blocking links from the ticket's TYPE TIER (`_TYPE_TIER`, `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:26`) instead of from its position in the parent hierarchy. Bug jira-reb-1582 names the correct rule directly: comparability is structural, and any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency. This story supersedes both bugs and replaces the policy.

## Approach

Replace type-tier comparability with structural (nearest-common-ancestor) comparability; add a resolved-pair invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of how the edge was produced; then detect and repair the edges already written under the old rule.

Rejected alternative — keep the type tiers and special-case the failing shape by clamping promotion below the nearest common ancestor. That removes 1803's specific symptom but leaves comparability keyed on a ticket's *type*, so a task and a story that are genuine siblings still could not hold a direct dependency, and re-typing a ticket would silently rewrite the meaning of the dependency graph. jira-reb-1582 asks for the rule itself to change; patching the fallback at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:93` would leave the store's semantics wrong in the same way.

Rejected alternative — reject cross-subtree blocking links with an error instead of escalating them. Honest, but it breaks every caller relying on auto-escalation today, including the `link` MCP tool and the reconciler's inbound apply path (`rebar.link` at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`). Escalation is retained, and its existing machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) is kept as the loud signal.

## Success Criteria

- The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the parent hierarchy alone; `_TYPE_TIER` no longer participates in that decision.
- No blocking edge can exist between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant, by any path into the resolver.
- Blocking edges already written under the type-tier rule are detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass.
- The escalation contract callers depend on — auto-escalate a cross-subtree link, emit the redirect record — is unchanged.

## Decomposition

Two children, in dependency order:

1. **Structural comparability and the ancestor invariant** (leaf) — rewrites the resolver in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` and moves the redundancy guard in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` onto the resolved pair. This is the fix for both superseded bugs.
2. **`link-audit` detection and repair** (leaf) — a store-wide scan plus one-shot repair for edges written under the old rule. It declares `depends_on` child 1, because the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver and cannot be written before those semantics are final.

The split follows the deliverable seam: child 1 changes what a new link means, child 2 fixes data already on disk. Each lands as one reviewable change. Neither is large enough to split further, and combining them would put a store-wide data rewrite in the same change as the semantics that rewrite depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The repro from bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 (a task and a story that are both direct children of one epic) records the requested task-to-story edge unchanged and produces no epic-to-child edge; verified by the regression test added in child 1, run against the store fixture.
- [ ] The worked example from bug jira-reb-1582 resolves as that ticket specifies — Task D under Story C escalates to Story C when linked to Task B, while Task B to Story C records directly; verified by the regression test added in child 1.
- [ ] `rebar link-audit` run twice against this repository's own tracker reports a non-empty first pass and an empty second pass after its repair; verified by running the command twice and comparing the two reports.
- [ ] Both children are closed, each with its Gerrit change at `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`; verified by the change status in Gerrit before each close.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/` all pass; verified by running them in the worktree.
